chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Safwan handed me a letter from Musa ibn Bakr and said to me, 'This is my hearing from Musa ibn Bakr, which I read to him.' Inside it was: Musa ibn Bakr from Ali ibn Sa'id from Zurarah who said:

This is what there is no disagreement among our companions regarding from Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them) when asked about a woman who left behind a husband, a mother, and two daughters: 'The husband gets one-fourth, the mother gets one-sixth, and the two daughters get the remainder, because if they were two men, they would only get the remainder, and a woman is never given more than a man would get in her place.'

If the deceased left a mother or father, a wife, and a daughter, then the inheritance is from twenty-four parts: the wife gets one-eighth (three parts), one of the parents gets one-sixth (four parts), the daughter gets one-half (twelve parts), and the remaining five parts are returned to the shares of the daughter and one of the parents according to their shares, and nothing is returned to the wife.

If he left two parents, a wife, and a daughter, it is also from twenty-four parts: the two parents get two-sixths (eight parts, four for each), the wife gets one-eighth (three parts), the daughter gets one-half (twelve parts), and one remaining part is returned to the daughter and the two parents according to their shares, and nothing is returned to the wife.

If she left a father, a husband, and a daughter, the father gets two parts out of twelve (which is one-sixth), the husband gets one-fourth (three parts out of twelve), the daughter gets one-half (six parts out of twelve), and one remaining part is returned to the daughter and the father according to their shares, and nothing is returned to the husband.

And no one from God's creation inherits with a child except the two parents, the husband, and the wife. If he has no child, but the children of the child are male or female, they are like the children; they inherit the inheritance of sons. And the children of daughters are like the daughters; they inherit the inheritance of daughters. And they block the two parents, the husband, and the wife from their larger shares.
And if they descend through two or three or more generations, they inherit what the children of the body inherit, and they block what the children of the body block.

4 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari said: A dispute arose between two men from my uncles' sons regarding inheritance, so I sent a letter to him regarding that for them to issue a ruling based on his opinion. So they both wrote to him:

'May God make us your ransom, what do you say about a woman who left behind a husband, a daughter, and a sister from her father and mother?' And I said, 'May I be your ransom, if you see fit to answer us with the truth.'

So a letter came out to them: 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. May God grant us and you well-being, the best well-being. I understood your letter; you mentioned that a woman died and left behind a husband, a daughter, and a sister from her father and mother. So the ruling is: for the husband one-fourth, and what remains is for the daughter.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance shares for a wife, mother, and two daughters?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Saffan from Musa ibn Bakr, provides a detailed jurisprudential analysis of inheritance shares, emphasizing the principle that female descendants receive no more than the share of a male in equivalent positions. It further clarifies the mechanism of 'rad' (return of surplus) to daughters and parents while excluding spouses, and establishes the rule of 'hijab' (exclusion) where grandchildren inherit as if they were direct children, thereby blocking parents and spouses from their primary shares. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the consistency of the Quranic distribution model as interpreted by the Imams.
